name: user-walkthrough
description: Walk through an app or service as its user — actually launch and operate it (browser via Playwright, CLI, API), either as a persona doing concrete tasks or by following its README/manual procedure verbatim — to find usability friction, contradictions between screens or between docs and behaviour, unhelpful error messages, and bugs. By default the walk is delegated to a separate agent that has not read the source (a genuinely first-time user), and the conductor re-verifies every finding from a fresh state. Returns a severity-ranked report where every finding carries numbered reproduction steps, expected vs actual, observed evidence, and reproduction count, without changing the code. Bundles check_report.py (rejects findings without evidence, speculative 'actual' results, and Blockers nobody observed) with a three-direction test harness, plus an eval target app and README with seeded defects. Hands fixing to the developer or a dev skill, source review to code-reviewer, design direction to frontend-design.
